item.title: [general] How AI Assistants are Moving the Security Goalposts
item.description: AI-based assistants or "agents" -- autonomous programs that have access to the user's computer, files, online services and can automate virtually any task -- are growing in popularity with developers and IT workers. But as so many eyebrow-raising headlines over the past few weeks have shown, these powerful and assertive new tools are rapidly shifting the security priorities for organizations, while blurring the lines between data and code, trusted co-worker and insider threat, ninja hacker and novice code jockey.

item.title: [general] Unbreakable Enterprise Kernel 8.2 ships with confidential computing support, XFS live repair
item.description: <p>Many enterprise Linux deployments rely on hardware-level memory isolation to protect sensitive workloads from co-tenants and compromised hypervisors. Oracle&#8217;s Unbreakable Enterprise Kernel 8.2 (UEK 8.2) extends that capability on Oracle Linux with support for Intel Trust Domain Extensions, along with a set of file system and memory management changes intended to reduce downtime and improve diagnostic visibility. UEK 8.2 is based on the mainline long-term stable Linux 6.12 kernel and carries the release number 6.12.0-200. &#8230; <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/03/26/oracle-unbreakable-enterprise-kernel-8-2/" rel="nofollow">More <span class="meta-nav">&#8594;</span></a></p> <p>The post <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/03/26/oracle-unbreakable-enterprise-kernel-8-2/">Unbreakable Enterprise Kernel 8.2 ships with confidential computing support, XFS live repair</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com">Help Net Security</a>.</p>

item.title: [general] As the US Midterms Approach, AI Is Going to Emerge as a Key Issue Concerning Voters
item.description: <p>In December, the Trump administration signed an executive order that <a href="https://www.nytimes.com/2025/12/11/technology/ai-trump-executive-order.html">neutered</a> states&#8217; ability to regulate AI by ordering his administration to both sue and withhold funds from states that try to do so. This action pointedly supported <a href="https://www.nytimes.com/2025/12/08/us/politics/trump-executive-order-ai-laws.html">industry lobbyists</a> keen to avoid any constraints and consequences on their deployment of AI, while undermining the efforts of consumers, advocates, and industry associations concerned about AI&#8217;s harms who have spent years pushing for state regulation.</p> <p>Trump&#8217;s actions have clarified the ideological alignments around AI within America&#8217;s electoral factions. They set down lines on a new playing field for the midterm elections, prompting members of his party, the opposition, and all of us to consider where we stand in the debate over how and where to let AI transform our lives...</p>
